statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-34182 (OpenSSL security advisory of 9 June 2026): CMS processing does not check the cipher and tag length of AuthEnvelopedData, so CMS_decrypt() can accept a message re-encrypted under a non-AEAD cipher or with a shortened tag, letting an attacker forge messages or use the result as a decryption oracle. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.6 are affected and 3.5.7 fixes it; the FIPS modules are not affected. The fix on the openssl-3.5 branch is commit 7947e6a, which makes crypto/cms/cms_enc.c reject a non-AEAD cipher for AuthEnvelopedData and tag lengths outside 4 to 16 bytes: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/7947e6a81eb8776802f159fb6762cb7fcf7e34c7. Checked the libcrypto3 package of every openssl build published for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, each against the index checksum. The libcrypto.so.3 version string is OpenSSL 3.5.4, 3.5.5 or 3.5.6 in 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0 and 3.5.6-r1, and OpenSSL 3.5.7 or later in 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2. So 3.5.7-r0 is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-34182 (OpenSSL security advisory of 9 June 2026): CMS processing does not check the cipher and tag length of AuthEnvelopedData, so CMS_decrypt() can accept a message re-encrypted under a non-AEAD cipher or with a shortened tag, letting an attacker forge messages or use the result as a decryption oracle. OpenSSL 3.5.0 to 3.5.6 are affected and 3.5.7 fixes it; the FIPS modules are not affected. The fix on the openssl-3.5 branch is commit 7947e6a, which makes crypto/cms/cms_enc.c reject a non-AEAD cipher for AuthEnvelopedData and tag lengths outside 4 to 16 bytes: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/7947e6a81eb8776802f159fb6762cb7fcf7e34c7. Debian fixed it in trixie in 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 (DSA-6335-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-34182. Every DHI Debian 13 openssl build is built from Debian's trixie source. Checked the libssl3t64 package, which holds libcrypto.so.3, of every published build for amd64 and arm64, each against the index SHA256: the builds from 3.5.5-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, including their +fips builds, carry no changelog entry for this CVE, and every build from 3.5.6-1~deb13u2+dhi0 on, through 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 and including their +fips builds, lists the CVE in its changelog entry for the 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 security update. The fix makes no visible string change, but the same security update's fix for CVE-2026-34181 is visible in libcrypto.so.3 (its new error text) in exactly these builds and in none of the earlier ones. The +fips builds compile libcrypto.so.3 from the same Debian source, and their FIPS provider is outside the affected code. So 3.5.6-1~deb13u2+dhi0 is the first fixed build.
